jessica_cust: Hey folks — after upgrading to embed-sdk v1.4.2 our indexer started throwing dimension-mismatch errors. Expected 1536 but seeing intermittent vectors with length 0 or 384. Happens during high throughput runs (3k docs, batch_size=32). Any known regressions?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, @jessica_cust. Can you paste the client code + the raw API response for one of the failing requests? Also which model and region?

jessica_cust: model=all-mpnet-base-v2 (redwood-hosted), region=us-west-2. Here's simplified repro (python):

```python
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key=...)
batcher = client.new_batcher(batch_size=32, timeout_ms=250)
for doc in docs:
    batcher.add(doc.text)
# observe: occasional responses where len(vec) != 1536
```

and a sample API body we logged (server response header only):
`200 OK`
`application/json`
`{"data":[{"id":"0","embedding":[...1536 floats...]},{"id":"1","embedding":[]},{"id":"2","embedding":[...384 floats...]}]}`

ryan_sdk: Thanks for the repro. Two quick q's: are you using the python SDK's built-in retry/backoff configs? Any custom concurrency or manual threading around the batcher?

jessica_cust: default retry settings, no extra threads. We do set batcher.max_inflight=4.

observability_bot: metric spike detected: "embed.batcher.flush_on_timeout" events increased at 2026-03-16T14:02:43Z. 95th latency 1.25s, 5xx rate 0.4% (brief).

maya_enginfra: hypothesis: if the client times out waiting for a batch and triggers a retry, the batcher may be flushing a partially-populated buffer or reusing an internal buffer incorrectly, causing truncated payloads reaching the model runtime. The runtime may then return shorter embeddings (or empty entries) which our response-assembler maps back to client items mismatched by index.

alex_support: @maya_enginfra, do we have server-side logs correlating to these request IDs? @jessica_cust can you share a request_id from one failing response?

jessica_cust: sure — request_id=rp_20260316_usw2_9f3b2. Attached logs show the server accepted a payload of 8192 bytes and returned a response array length 32, but some items had empty embedding arrays.

ryan_sdk: I reproduced locally with a stress test. Root cause looks like a race in the SDK's batcher: when a request times out, the retry path re-enqueues items but an internal slice that holds embeddings gets reused before the response mapping completes, so indices can shift. We'll push a hotfix to ensure: 1) atomic snapshot of pending batch before send, 2) pre-send validation that payload shape matches expected ids, 3) disable reusing internal buffers for in-flight batches.

alex_support: thanks — rough ETA? Any recommended immediate workarounds for customers?

ryan_sdk: patch ready, running unit + stress tests. If all green, we'll roll a patch to v1.4.3 today. Short-term workaround: set batcher.timeout_ms to 1000 to avoid timeout-triggered retries, or set batcher.max_inflight=1 to reduce concurrency races. Also add a client-side assert: after receiving embeddings, validate len(vec)==expected_dim and retry the whole document (not partial batch) if mismatch.

jessica_cust: increased timeout to 1000ms and ran the job — no mismatches in ~6k docs. Good for now. Please share the patch when available so we can upgrade safely.

maya_enginfra: we'll also add a server-side defensive check: if any embedding in a response has dimensionality != expected, mark request for deeper trace and surface an error instead of silently returning shorter vectors. That will help catch regressions faster.

alex_support: Action items: 1) @ryan_sdk publish v1.4.3 with batcher atomic-snapshot + buffer isolation (target: today EOD), 2) @eng-infra add server-side dim-validation (target: next sprint), 3) @jessica_cust follow up after upgrading. Closing loop once patch verified. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jessica_cust: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround!
